rows.claim: The operative TDD loop is red -> green, with refactoring outside the loop.
rows.adjudication: Operative SKILL.md plus changelog agree on red->green; README/bucket/Codex descriptions retain red-green-refactor. Prompt behavior is not machine-enforced.
rows.next_evidence: Later current-state comparison and runtime adherence belong to later verification gates.

rows.claim: Human docs accurately describe the promoted set and invocation split.
rows.adjudication: Generated frozen distribution truth is 25 promoted with 14 user-invoked/11 model-invoked; ask-matt human docs retain 22/13 wording.
rows.next_evidence: No runtime reproduction needed to prove frozen numerical drift; later compare post-frozen current docs if relevant.

rows.claim: Load-bearing behavior claims are verified by reading the target SKILL.md rather than trusting the router summary.
rows.adjudication: Human docs demand trace evidence of target-source reading; operative ask-matt has no mandatory target-source-read step. The documented verification criterion is not enforced in the operative prompt.
rows.next_evidence: Determine whether this is intentional accepted design or should become an operative gate.

rows.claim: Release/package metadata has one coherent version authority.
rows.adjudication: package.json -> plugin.json synchronization is executable/release-wired, but package-lock root metadata remains 0.0.0 and is outside the sync script. Direct frozen runtime observation: the stale 0.0.0 lock metadata was reproduced; npm pack selected package.json version 1.2.3, and an offline package-lock-only normalization rewrote both root lock version fields to 1.2.3.
rows.next_evidence: Release-path observation remains separate under B-029; local npm behavior shows the stale root lock version is normalized and does not control npm pack versioning.

rows.claim: The canonical glossary format participates in the operative Teach workflow.
rows.adjudication: The support format exists and human docs describe it, but operative Teach does not load/reference it. The file is not a source-tree orphan; the operative linkage is missing.
rows.next_evidence: Classify optional/manual behavior as accepted design or wire/retire the support format.

rows.claim: Teach writes learner state into the intended user workspace rather than installed skill storage.
rows.adjudication: Frozen source mixes co-located support references and relative workspace paths; reported issue evidence exists, but source inspection alone cannot settle harness working-directory resolution.
rows.next_evidence: Reproduce in a supported harness or obtain equivalent direct runtime evidence.

rows.claim: Diagnosing-bugs includes explicit artifact/output redaction safeguards.
rows.adjudication: Operative skill and changelog contain shipped redaction instructions while human docs still call the behavior unimplemented. Enforcement remains prompt-level, not a deterministic sanitizer.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime adherence is a later verification question; frozen docs drift is already established.

rows.claim: The generated architecture report is self-contained in a dependency-independent sense.
rows.adjudication: Direct isolated runtime observation confirms the report is a single HTML file but not dependency-independent: the frozen Tailwind and Mermaid external requests are required and both fail in a controlled offline fixture.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime closure covers the frozen CDN dependency boundary only. Define whether the product intends packaging self-containment or offline/locked-down portability; a real-browser rendering check can broaden compatibility evidence later.

rows.claim: Diagnosing-bugs autonomously hands architecture findings to improve-codebase-architecture.
rows.adjudication: The autonomous handoff was deliberately removed and is absent from diagnosing-bugs, but human docs and ask-matt retain it.
rows.next_evidence: Secondary surfaces should be aligned or explicitly historical.

rows.claim: Implement's required final code review can see the implementation it is asked to review before commit.
rows.adjudication: Direct synthetic git-runtime observation confirms the pre-commit gap: Implement orders code-review before commit, while code-review's fixed-point...HEAD precondition is empty until the implementation is committed. The working-tree change exists but is outside the mandated review diff.
rows.next_evidence: Frozen behavior is runtime-observed. A source correction would require committing before review or teaching code-review an explicit working-tree review mode.

rows.claim: The in-progress bucket README accurately describes retro's implementation maturity.
rows.adjudication: Bucket README says STUB/nonfunctional; operative retro source contains a substantial multi-step workflow and cross-skill call.
rows.next_evidence: Align maturity description; end-to-end quality remains a separate runtime question.

rows.claim: The skill's stated four error-level rules exactly describe the shipped dependency-cruiser enforcement and package-local freedom.
rows.adjudication: Static inspection established that SKILL.md says four error rules and unconditional intra-package freedom while the shipped config contains five. Synthetic-consumer runtime now confirms the extra tests-folder-is-private rule bites: same-package non-test code importing its own tests/ fixture fails under that fifth rule. The prose/config mismatch is both static and operational; CT-012 remains open.
rows.next_evidence: Source-side correction remains: document five rules plus the tests/ exception, or change the config/prose so the four-rule model is exact. Frozen runtime behavior is now observed.

rows.claim: Execution enters a Wayfinder map only through an independently authorized override rather than the guarded agent relaxing its own constraint.
rows.adjudication: The planning default explicitly permits an execution-carrying Notes override, while charting instructs the same agent to create the map with Notes filled in. No independent user-confirmation/authority check is specified for that override.
rows.next_evidence: Require/identify an independent override authority or classify self-authored override as accepted design.

rows.claim: Completion requires evidence that the boundary checker actually rejects a deliberate deep import.
rows.adjudication: The skill's proof-of-enforcement completion criterion is directly runtime-observed in a disposable synthetic TypeScript consumer using the exact frozen config: clean pass, temporary tests/example.test.ts -> ../lib/impl failure specifically under tests-through-entrypoints, then clean pass after revert.
rows.next_evidence: Representative runtime completion semantics are closed. Broader compatibility across package managers and unusual repository layouts remains a separate generalization question.

rows.claim: Generated wizard scripts receive static shell validation before handoff.
rows.adjudication: Wizard requires bash -n and shellcheck when available, but explicitly does not require an end-to-end agent execution. Static syntax/lint proof is stronger than prose-only but weaker than runtime observation. Direct frozen runtime observation: bash syntax passed; the shipped example completed with synthetic values, wrote the expected env entries without echoing the dummy secret, and preserved existing values on rerun.
rows.next_evidence: Red-team generated wizard variants and browser-step accuracy later; this runtime observation covers the shipped template library/example only.

rows.claim: The Claude Code hook blocks the listed dangerous Git command strings.
rows.adjudication: The hook exits 2 on its regex-matched command patterns and setup requires a synthetic blocked-command test. Enforcement is executable but heuristic string matching, not parsed shell/Git semantics.
rows.next_evidence: Red-team equivalent/wrapped commands and false-positive strings in Phase 9/runtime testing.

rows.claim: Pre-commit setup proves installed hooks execute through a real commit.
rows.adjudication: The frozen setup-pre-commit workflow is directly runtime-observed in a disposable npm/git repository. Husky initialization created prepare=husky and executable Git-hook shim plumbing; manual lint-staged formatted a staged file; then an actual commit using the documented message ran lint-staged, typecheck, and tests, formatted and re-staged a hook-only target, and completed cleanly. One frozen verification predicate is stale against the resolved Husky version: the generated .husky/pre-commit user file is not executable, while the executable .husky/_/pre-commit shim invokes it through sh -e. Functional hook execution still succeeds.
rows.next_evidence: Representative npm end-to-end smoke is closed. Preserve the executable-bit predicate mismatch as toolchain drift; package-manager variants and future upstream Husky/lint-staged compatibility remain separate generalization/current-state questions.

rows.claim: Release versioning keeps package.json and Claude plugin version synchronized.
rows.adjudication: npm run version invokes sync-plugin-version.mjs and the release workflow uses that command; --check detects drift. This closes plugin/package drift statically while leaving package-lock outside the mechanism (B-004/CT-004). Direct frozen runtime observation: --check passed in sync, failed on synthetic drift, and the executable repaired plugin.json to package.json without package-lock.json present.
rows.next_evidence: Observe a live Changesets release/version-PR path later; B-004 separately tracks package-lock version truth.

rows.claim: Maintainer local linking includes engineering, productivity and in-progress skills while excluding misc/deprecated.
rows.adjudication: The executable find expression explicitly excludes deprecated and misc and otherwise discovers SKILL.md under skills/, yielding the generated 33-skill local-link set.
rows.next_evidence: Filesystem symlink behavior can be runtime-observed later; static selection semantics are closed.

rows.claim: The maintainer listing utility enumerates every current SKILL.md in the repository tree.
rows.adjudication: The script runs find from the repository root for SKILL.md, excluding only node_modules, and sorts the result; frozen generated distribution truth therefore treats all 37 current skills as list-visible.
rows.next_evidence: No separate runtime verification is needed for static selection semantics unless environment-specific find behavior becomes material.

rows.claim: Setup presents the generated configuration to the user for editing before it writes repository files.
rows.adjudication: The operative setup workflow explicitly requires showing the Agent skills block plus docs/agents drafts and letting the user edit them before the write step. This is a clear human checkpoint, but it is prompt-level rather than mechanically enforced.
rows.next_evidence: Later runtime observation can test whether supported harnesses consistently honor the checkpoint.

rows.claim: Setup verification is intentionally handled through the same prompt-driven skill rather than a separate deterministic verify/check command.
rows.adjudication: The negative-memory policy explicitly rejects a separate verify/check mode and says maintainers should invoke setup with a natural-language verification request. The operative skill is explicitly prompt-driven, so this is intentional design rather than a missing implementation accidentally presented as deterministic validation.
rows.next_evidence: A later runtime pass can test verification quality, but static design intent is reconciled.

rows.claim: Diagnosing-bugs does not proceed to hypothesis work before a tight red-capable feedback command exists and has been run.
rows.adjudication: The operative skill repeatedly states no red-capable command means no Phase 2, requires one command already run with output, and instructs the agent to stop if it starts theorizing first. This is unusually strong prompt gating, but there is no external machine state preventing a model from skipping it.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime/red-team testing should attempt to induce premature hypothesis generation and measure adherence.

rows.claim: Every triaged item maintains exactly one category role and exactly one state role.
rows.adjudication: Triage explicitly states the one-category/one-state invariant and tells the agent to stop on pre-existing state-role conflicts. Generic GitHub labels are demonstrably additive in the isolated fixture, but the fixture could not create the frozen skill's exact custom canonical state labels; that supporting tracker observation does not establish the required role-transition behavior. The invariant therefore remains a prompt-level weakness, not a runtime-promoted finding.
rows.next_evidence: Use a disposable tracker fixture that can create the exact canonical role labels, begin with an actual frozen state-role label, then observe whether an additive quick override leaves the prior state label in place. The current generic-label fixture is supporting-only.

rows.claim: Normal triage verifies the issue/PR claim against code or executable behavior before grilling it into a specification.
rows.adjudication: The operative sequence is gather context -> recommend/wait -> verify claim -> grill if needed -> apply outcome. Bugs should be reproduced; PRs should be checked out and tested. A separately documented maintainer quick override intentionally bypasses grilling and normal verification, so this row applies to the normal triage path only.
rows.next_evidence: Later runtime observation can test whether the normal path actually performs the requested reproduction/checkout before grilling.

rows.claim: Implement-spec dispatches only tickets on the currently unblocked task-graph frontier and expands concurrency as dependencies clear.
rows.adjudication: The skill explicitly defines tickets as a blocking task graph, dispatches implementer subagents from the frontier, and asks for more dispatch when merges change that frontier. There is no executable scheduler or machine check of dependency legality; correctness depends on agent interpretation of ticket relationships at runtime.
rows.next_evidence: Run a representative dependency graph with at least one blocked branch and verify that no blocked ticket starts early.

rows.claim: Changes made to fix final code-review findings are themselves revalidated before the PR is marked ready.
rows.adjudication: Implement-spec requires one final /code-review, then delegates all review fixes to a single implementer subagent and immediately advances to marking the PR ready. No second review, finding-by-finding check, test gate, or equivalent post-fix acceptance step is required for the changed branch.
rows.next_evidence: Add or identify a post-fix acceptance gate; runtime reproduction can demonstrate whether review-fix regressions can reach the ready state.

rows.claim: Resolved domain terms are captured immediately in CONTEXT.md, while ADR creation is reserved for hard-to-reverse, surprising, genuine trade-off decisions.
rows.adjudication: The operative skill distinguishes active model changes from passive vocabulary reading, requires immediate CONTEXT.md updates when a term is resolved, constrains CONTEXT.md to glossary content, and offers ADRs only when all three stated criteria are met. All of these controls are prompt-level.
rows.next_evidence: Second-pass/runtime testing should look for implementation-detail leakage into CONTEXT.md and over-eager ADR creation.

rows.claim: Main-branch release automation routes versioning through Changesets and the repository's npm version command before tag publication.
rows.adjudication: Frozen-source configuration establishes the intended Changesets version/tag route. An actual GitHub Actions Release run at the exact frozen commit completed its Version job, including Checkout, Node setup, npm ci, and the configured Create Version Pull Request action. The retained job metadata proves this path executed; it does not expose whether the run had a pending changeset or emitted a tag, so no claim of publication is made.
rows.next_evidence: Frozen Release workflow execution is observed. If needed, obtain an upstream action log or output that proves a pending-changeset run created a version PR and/or emitted a tag; that broader branch evidence is not inferred here.

rows.claim: The parent spec's ready-for-agent label is safely distinguishable from executable ticket slices for AFK dispatch.
rows.adjudication: to-spec automatically applies ready-for-agent to the parent spec. Its own human docs explicitly state that AFK pollers cannot see the intended input-vs-work distinction and may build the whole spec; to-tickets is instructed not to modify the parent, so the chain contains no operative cleanup/disambiguation step.
rows.next_evidence: Use a distinct parent/spec state, strip ready-for-agent during ticketization, or make dispatchers mechanically distinguish parent specs from executable tickets.

rows.claim: The ticket breakdown and blocking edges are approved by the user before tracker publication.
rows.adjudication: Both the operative skill and human docs require the numbered ticket breakdown, blocker review, merge/split feedback, and user approval before tracker publication. This is a clear human checkpoint but remains prompt-enforced.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test whether ambiguous or AFK prompts can cause publication before explicit approval.

rows.claim: Each ticket's acceptance criteria are falsifiable and red at the implementer's base state unless explicitly justified.
rows.adjudication: The operative ticket templates require checkboxes but no red-at-base/falsifiability proof. Human docs explicitly identify criteria already true at base, dependent on other tickets, or merely restating the request, and recommend a manual falsifying-observation check that is absent from SKILL.md.
rows.next_evidence: Require every criterion to name a falsifying observation and verify it is false at base unless explicitly justified.

rows.area: implement ticket lifecycle and frontier closure
rows.claim: Completing a ticket through implement publishes the completion state needed to unblock dependent tickets.
rows.adjudication: to-tickets models execution as blocker completion/closure, but implement ends at commit and has no work-item close/check-off step. Human implement docs explicitly warn that dependency chains therefore do not visibly unblock without manual state repair.
rows.next_evidence: Add an explicit completion step that reconciles acceptance criteria and closes/updates the ticket before frontier recomputation.

rows.claim: Research traces claims to primary sources and persists a cited Markdown artifact in the repository.
rows.adjudication: The research skill explicitly requires first-party primary sources, tracing every claim to the owning source, and writing one cited Markdown file using the repository's existing notes convention. The requirements are prompt-level and depend on actual source access/runtime behavior.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime/red-team should inject plausible secondary sources and unsupported claims to measure adherence.

rows.claim: Prototype code remains off main while validated learning and a pointer to the prototype are preserved.
rows.adjudication: The operative prototype skill requires throwaway naming, minimal polish/persistence, folding the validated decision into real code, then committing the prototype to a throwaway branch out of main and leaving a pointer on the implementation issue. Whether those repository operations occur correctly cannot be settled statically.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-verify branch isolation, pointer creation, and decision capture on representative logic and UI prototypes.

rows.claim: Codebase-design consistently uses its defined module/interface/seam/adapter vocabulary and rejected alternatives.
rows.adjudication: The operative skill defines and explicitly requires exact terminology, including rejected alternatives such as component/service/API/boundary in the relevant meanings. This is internally coherent but entirely prompt-enforced.
rows.next_evidence: Second-pass/red-team should look for internal examples or linked support guidance that violate the stated vocabulary/seam rules.

rows.claim: The triage labels written into setup configuration are guaranteed to exist and be usable on the configured tracker.
rows.adjudication: Setup writes the role-to-label mapping and tracker templates document label operations, but the operative setup flow contains no explicit create-or-verify-label step. Static source alone does not establish whether pre-existing labels are guaranteed or how each supported tracker behaves when a configured label is absent.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test setup on a tracker lacking the default labels and observe whether later triage operations fail, create labels, or recover.

rows.claim: Every issue or PR entering ready-for-agent has the authoritative agent brief required for AFK execution.
rows.adjudication: AGENT-BRIEF.md defines the brief as the authoritative contract posted when an item moves to ready-for-agent, and the normal triage outcome requires it. The quick override applies ready-for-agent directly and only asks afterward whether the maintainer wants a brief, making the contract optional on that path.
rows.next_evidence: Require the brief before or atomically with ready-for-agent, or explicitly redefine the quick-override state and downstream consumer contract.

rows.claim: grill-with-docs composes grilling and domain-modeling rather than reimplementing either workflow.
rows.adjudication: The operative wrapper contains only two Skill-tool calls, one to `grilling` and one to `domain-modeling`. Phase 3 invocation joining found no illegal current operative call, so the composition is statically coherent and intentionally delegates behavior to the two target skills.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime observation can later test whether both delegated workflows are actually invoked and preserve their respective contracts in one session.

rows.claim: Conflict resolution reconstructs both sides' intent, resolves every hunk without aborting, runs project checks, and finishes the merge/rebase.
rows.adjudication: The skill has a coherent five-step contract: inspect state, trace primary-source intent, preserve both intents where possible without inventing behavior, run discovered checks, then stage/commit or continue rebase. `Never --abort` is an explicit design rule rather than an implicit fallback.
rows.next_evidence: Red-team a conflict where intents are genuinely incompatible and a rebase with multiple conflict stops; verify the skill neither invents behavior nor exits prematurely.

rows.claim: A conversation handoff is redacted, de-duplicated against durable artifacts, and launched immediately as a named background Claude agent in the current working directory.
rows.adjudication: The source explicitly requires redaction, pointer-over-duplication, suggested skills, a descriptive `--name`, and direct `claude --bg` launch. None of those privacy/completeness properties is enforced by a deterministic sanitizer or launcher owned by this repository, and successful behavior depends on the external Claude CLI/runtime.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test launch, working-directory inheritance, name propagation, artifact references, and deliberate secret/PII injection before treating the handoff as verified.

rows.claim: loop-me keeps `workflows/*.md` as the source of truth and continues grilling until an implementer could build the workflow without asking a question.
rows.adjudication: The skill explicitly separates loop vocabulary from mandatory structure, declares workflow files authoritative, and gives a demanding completion criterion: nothing is done while an implementation question remains. The stateful grilling dependency is prompt-mediated, not mechanically checked.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime/red-team with an underspecified workflow and verify the session refuses to declare done while implementation questions remain.

rows.claim: writing-beats writes only user-selected reachable beats, re-reading the article before each write and never writing ahead of the user's choice.
rows.adjudication: The operative workflow establishes prerequisites, restricts candidates to already-grounded concepts, requires the user to choose, writes one beat only, re-reads from disk, and repeats. User edits are explicitly preserved and may change subsequent routing.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test an attempted ungrounded beat and an external edit between turns; verify the candidate is blocked or grounded first and the edit is preserved.

rows.claim: writing-fragments captures raw material without imposing article structure and preserves user edits by re-reading before every append.
rows.adjudication: The skill explicitly separates explore from exploit, bans outlines/phases, defines a minimal fragment file format, captures from the initial prompt, and requires re-reading before writes. It permits targeted edits only on user request rather than blind overwrite.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test whether the agent resists outlining pressure and preserves reordered/deleted fragments made outside the conversation.

rows.claim: writing-shape treats the raw-material file as read-only and grows a separate article incrementally from user-agreed blocks.
rows.adjudication: The source requires a full initial read, a separate output path, explicit opening choice, grounded paragraph/block progression, immediate append after agreement, and re-read-before-write behavior while declaring the raw pile read-only.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test with external edits to both raw and output files and verify the raw source is never modified while article edits are preserved.

rows.claim: The migration's discovery command finds the assertion forms the skill promises to replace, including `as unknown as Type`.
rows.adjudication: Exact frozen-command reproduction disproved the earlier discovery-gap hypothesis. The grep searches each whole line; a documented `as unknown as Request` fixture is returned because its second ` as Request` substring satisfies ` as [A-Z]`. A lowercase-target control (`as request`) did not match. The discovery command therefore covers both advertised assertion forms, although the subsequent migration edits remain prompt-driven rather than mechanically guaranteed.
rows.next_evidence: If deeper verification is needed, test the actual edit/import/type-check migration on representative single- and double-assertion files; discovery coverage itself is closed.

rows.claim: The variant combinations described as valid by scaffold-exercises match the combinations its mandatory linter accepts.
rows.adjudication: Frozen scaffold-exercises permits a solution-only exercise, but isolated execution of the exact external ai-hero-cli v0.2.8 linter selected by the public course lock rejects a solution-only readme fixture with the stated missing-primary-variant error. An explainer-only control passes. The prompt/linter mismatch is operational; CT-020 remains open.
rows.next_evidence: Frozen behavior is runtime-observed. Source-side correction must make the allowed-variant prose and mandatory linter acceptance set identical, then rerun solution-only and explainer-only fixtures.

rows.claim: grill-me is only a user-invoked alias into the canonical grilling workflow rather than a second implementation of grilling semantics.
rows.adjudication: The entire operative body is a single call to `grilling`; this avoids duplicated interviewing logic and keeps grilling semantics in one source. Phase 3 invocation-policy joining found this current call legal.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime observation only needs to confirm the alias actually delegates rather than diverging in the host harness.

rows.claim: grilling asks only currently unblocked decisions, obtains facts itself, leaves decisions to the user, and stops only after the frontier is empty and the user confirms shared understanding.
rows.adjudication: The design-tree/frontier model explicitly delays dependent questions, asks the whole current frontier in rounds, delegates fact-finding rather than asking the user, and keeps actual decisions with the user. Completion requires both an empty frontier and user confirmation.
rows.next_evidence: Red-team with dependent questions and unavailable facts; verify downstream questions wait while unrelated frontier questions continue.

rows.claim: handoff writes a redacted pointer-rich continuation document to the operating system's temporary directory rather than the current workspace.
rows.adjudication: The skill explicitly requires OS-temp placement, sensitive-data redaction, suggested skills, and references instead of duplicating existing artifacts. It contains no deterministic redactor or temp-path resolver, so actual placement and redaction completeness remain runtime behaviors.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test platform-specific temp resolution plus seeded secrets/PII and verify the workspace remains untouched.

rows.claim: to-questionnaire interviews only for recipient/send context and required outputs, then produces one-question-per-idea coverage for every requested information gap.
rows.adjudication: The workflow separates who receives the document from what the user needs back, defines done for each intake step, and closes only when every named need is covered by a question in the written Markdown artifact. The one-idea-per-question rule is explicit.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test a multi-gap request and verify no requested gap disappears and no compound questions merge independent decisions.

rows.claim: wait-what re-pitches the prior explanation with additional context, ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, and the repository's ubiquitous language when context documents exist.
rows.adjudication: The skill is a concise prompt contract with three simultaneous constraints: add context, use ASD-STE100, and load ubiquitous language from CONTEXT.md/CONTEXT-MAP.md. No deterministic checker verifies controlled-language compliance or context-map resolution.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test in single-context, multi-context, and no-CONTEXT repositories; decide whether missing context needs an explicit fallback contract.

rows.claim: agent-facing documents use one source of truth, strong conditional context pointers, explicit completion criteria, progressive disclosure, and pruning rather than duplicating environment facts.
rows.adjudication: The skill and its mechanics support file present a coherent doctrine around context/cognitive load, information hierarchy, pointer wording, completion-criterion clarity/demand, leading words, positive steering, single-source truth, environment-as-source, pruning, and no-op deletion.
rows.next_evidence: Second-pass/red-team should apply the doctrine back onto the repository itself and record where shipped skills violate their own writing guidance.

rows.claim: Every current skill has Codex metadata whose implicit-invocation policy agrees with the frozen Claude invocation class: user-invoked skills opt out of implicit invocation, while model-invoked skills do not carry that opt-out.
rows.adjudication: All 37 current skills have agents/openai.yaml metadata. The completed Phase 3 invocation join found 37/37 policies joined and zero Claude-to-Codex invocation mismatches. Frozen user-invoked examples explicitly set policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false; model-invoked examples omit that opt-out. The metadata is machine-readable, but this audit has not yet observed an actual Codex runtime loading and obeying every file.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-observe representative user-invoked and model-invoked skills in Codex, then sample boundary cases if the harness behavior differs from the static contract.

rows.claim: The marketplace descriptor exposes one mattpocock-skills plugin sourced from the repository root and presents it as an installable Claude Code engineering-skills plugin.
rows.adjudication: The frozen marketplace.json contains a single plugin named mattpocock-skills with source './' and an engineering-skills description. This is machine-readable distribution metadata, but successful marketplace installation has not been runtime-observed in this audit.
rows.next_evidence: Exercise marketplace discovery/install against the frozen-compatible distribution path during Phase 7 runtime verification.

rows.claim: The HITL helper mechanically pauses for user actions and captures observations for the agent, while secret-sensitive guidance such as leaving sign-in to a non-captured step is advisory rather than technically enforced.
rows.adjudication: The shell functions step() and capture() mechanically block on terminal input and print captured values at the end. The file explicitly warns that capture echoes values back to the terminal and says signing in should remain a step, but nothing in the function prevents a caller from capturing a secret. The safety boundary therefore depends on correct template editing. Direct frozen runtime observation: the HITL shell template passed syntax and completed a benign synthetic interaction, emitting captured values exactly as documented.
rows.next_evidence: Red-team secret/PII misuse and shell-input edge cases later; do not use real credentials.

rows.claim: At a phase boundary the documented decision tree checks Continue, /clear, /handoff, subagent, then /compact in that order, treating every non-Continue transition as a lossy conversion from primary to secondary context.
rows.adjudication: PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md explicitly defines the five options, states that the first yes wins, places /compact last as the default rather than first reach, and explains the primary-to-secondary information loss. These are judgement/prompt rules, not executable policy.
rows.next_evidence: Later compare real routing decisions against this ordered tree during red-team verification, especially ambiguous boundaries.

rows.claim: Engineering exploration should read relevant CONTEXT/CONTEXT-MAP and ADR material when present, proceed silently when absent, use glossary vocabulary, and surface ADR conflicts instead of silently overriding them.
rows.adjudication: domain.md gives explicit before-exploring reads, absence handling, glossary vocabulary rules, and ADR-conflict behavior. No executable checker enforces those obligations.
rows.next_evidence: Observe a setup/exploration run in repos with present, absent, and conflicting domain docs.

rows.claim: The local tracker stores specs and one-file-per-ticket issues under .scratch, uses explicit Status/Type/Blocked-by fields, and defines claim-before-work plus resolve-and-link-back semantics for wayfinding.
rows.adjudication: issue-tracker-local.md defines exact paths, numbering, state fields, frontier scan, claiming, resolution and map update behavior. The contract is procedural; no parser or lock is provided here to enforce atomic claims or valid state transitions.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-test concurrent/duplicate claiming and malformed status files before treating the local tracker as robust coordination machinery.

rows.claim: Mocks are reserved for system boundaries; internal collaborators and owned modules should not be mocked, and external interfaces should be designed for narrow dependency injection.
rows.adjudication: mocking.md clearly separates system-boundary mocks from internal collaborators and gives dependency-injection/SDK-style guidance. There is no static test-lint rule in this surface that prevents internal mocking.
rows.next_evidence: Red-team the TDD workflow with codebases that already use internal mocks and see whether the operative skill follows or overrides this support rule.

rows.claim: Tests should verify observable behavior through public interfaces, avoid implementation-detail and tautological assertions, and survive internal refactors.
rows.adjudication: tests.md defines good integration-style behavior tests and concrete red flags for implementation-detail, external-bypass and tautological tests. These standards are guidance rather than a machine-enforced test-quality gate.
rows.next_evidence: Use adversarial examples during Phase 9 to test whether the operative TDD skill rejects brittle tests that still pass.

rows.claim: Rejected enhancements are persisted one file per concept under .out-of-scope, consulted by semantic concept similarity on future requests, and changed only with maintainer confirmation/reconsideration.
rows.adjudication: OUT-OF-SCOPE.md defines durable rejection records, semantic deduplication, maintainer confirm/reconsider/disagree branches, and the narrow write condition of rejected enhancement-as-wontfix. Matching and record maintenance are agent judgement, not executable enforcement.
rows.next_evidence: Test near-duplicate and superficially similar requests to measure false-positive/false-negative semantic matching during red-team verification.

rows.claim: Learning records are created lazily, numbered sequentially, capture demonstrated non-trivial understanding or prior knowledge rather than mere coverage, and preserve superseded understanding instead of deleting it.
rows.adjudication: LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md defines lazy creation, sequential numbering, evidence-oriented write conditions, non-qualifying cases, and supersession. No schema validator or numbering lock is supplied by this file.
rows.next_evidence: Observe Teach across repeated sessions, including a corrected misconception and concurrent/new record numbering edge case.

rows.claim: A teaching workspace has one concise, concrete mission whose why, observable success criteria, constraints and out-of-scope boundaries steer subsequent teaching and are revised when reality changes.
rows.adjudication: MISSION-FORMAT.md defines the workspace-root artifact, template and rules including one mission per workspace, concrete outcomes, pushback on vagueness, revision on goal shift and brevity. These are prompt-level constraints.
rows.next_evidence: Runtime-observe mission creation and a mid-course mission change to verify downstream teaching actually reorients.

rows.claim: Explainer knowledge should come from curated high-trust resources, wisdom from listed communities, every resource should be annotated, gaps made explicit, weak sources pruned, and community opt-outs remembered.
rows.adjudication: RESOURCES-FORMAT.md explicitly says knowledge should be drawn from the curated file rather than parametric guesses, separates Knowledge and Wisdom, requires annotations, gaps and pruning, and records community preferences. Source quality and community usefulness still depend on external evidence and agent judgement.
rows.next_evidence: Test Teach on a topic with incomplete resources to verify it surfaces gaps rather than filling them from unsupported model guesses.
